thread:
Maria: FYI were getting p95 regressions after the v2.14.4 canary rollout to cohort-3. Text-gen endpoints that pass through auth are hitting p95 ~450-500ms (was ~110ms). Tickets piling in.

Jon: Seeing that on the dashboard too. Spike at ~15:20 UTC aligns with the rollout. alert: canary-latency-p95. :warning:

incidents-bot: Alert fired: canary-p95-latency (svc: api-gen, threshold: 200ms)  15:22 UTC. Recommended runbook: eng-runtime/latency-bisect.

Kevin: Note that v2.14.4 includes the scheduler "latebinding" tweak and a reduced batch_timeout_ms=12. Hypothesis: scheduler now favours a fallback kernel on short requests when load briefly spikes, increasing queue time.

Leo: Quick local repro I ran:
```
# loadgen for short sequences (auth flows)
python tools/loadgen.py --model small-gpt --seq 64 --concurrency 35 --duration 240 --endpoint https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate --auth yes
```
Median unchanged (~90ms) but p95 jumps to 420-500ms when auth validation is in the path.

Maria: Adding traces: https://telemetry.redwood/s/trace/9f8e7d (sample 15:23 UTC). Trace shows long time in runtime queue before worker start.

Jon: KV cache metrics: auth-cache hit rate steady. Runtime queue_depth on canary hosts shows ~3-6s microbursts. Kernel scheduler stats show increased context-switch syscalls on hosts with v2.14.4.

Kevin: Did a quick commit bisect on the runtime image. Culprit narrowed to commit range abc1234..abc1238 where scheduler fallback logic was changed. The fallback picks a slower kernel variant under transient load if latebinding condition triggers.

Leo: Diff excerpt I pulled: 
```
- if (seq_len < 128) select fast_kernel();
+ if (system.load > HIGH) select fallback_kernel(); // latebinding change
```
So a short-request path now gets fallback_kernel when load spikes even briefly. With auth validation the extra latency compounds.

Maria: Immediate mitigation: rollback cohort-3 canary to v2.14.3. Initiating rollback via control plane. ETA ~5m.

CS Team: Notified impacted customers: "We're investigating increased latency and rolling back a recent runtime change. Will update in ~10m."

incidents-bot: Rollback job started by Maria. Job id: rb-2026-04-XX-007. Progress: 0/12 hosts.

Jon: After partial rollback (6/12) p95 started trending down. Full rollback completed at 15:38 UTC; p95 returned to ~120-160ms, p99 ~220-300ms.

Kevin: Post-rollback action items: revert the latebinding fallback or add a guard to avoid switching kernel for seq_len < 128 / auth-bound requests. Also add a canary e2e probe that simulates small, auth-bound concurrent traffic.

Leo: I added a repro script and a candidate fix branch fix/scheduler-fallback-auth with unit tests asserting kernel selection for short sequences under transient load. CI: https://ci.redwood/job/eng-runtime/7482.

Maria: Filing follow-ups: 
- KEVIN: PR to change fallback selector + integration tests (owner)
- LEO: Add canary e2e probe that runs small-seq auth workload for 10m pre-rollout (owner)
- JON: Update eng-runtime/latency-bisect runbook to include kernel-selector bisect checklist and short-seq probe steps
- CS TEAM: Customer follow-up and note about rollback mitigation

Jon: Note for postmortem: median latency unchanged so this could have slipped past naive canary checks. Lesson: canary workloads must include small, auth-validated requests at modest concurrency to surface kernel-selection regressions that only affect p95/p99.

Maria: Thanks all. If anyone sees residual customer reports, DM me. :thumbsup:
